criteria.detail: recorded FAIL because the outcome map was short a cell, not because the run was. Neither account registered for this arm survived and the reading landed in a third cell that had not been enumerated. With terms fixed by position the queue is frozen and unreached edges are 36.7 per cent. Letting terms **improve** with load, which is the sign this stage's own carrier has, moves that figure by nothing: the mean is 36.7 per cent at eta=-0.9 and it is above the frozen value in 0 of 20 seeds and below it in 0. That kills the account that scale reinforces concentration. It also kills the account that movement alone returns edges, because the negative side does move: distinct heads 2.00 against 1.00 and first-ten overlap 0.9953 against 1.0000. **What returns edges is eviction of the head and not movement in the queue.** The modal head holds 0.9548 of rounds at eta=-0.9 against 1.0000 frozen and 0.8538 at eta=+0.9, so improving a busy counterparty's terms pushes it further into a seat it already holds, because busy and well-positioned are the same node here. Asymmetry, for the record: at magnitude 0.9 the negative side reads +14.9 points against the positive

The baseline reads 36.34 per cent against 1/e at 36.788, a gap of 0.45 points, and the figure moves 14.5 points across the cells: baseline 36.3, out-degree x2 40.0, out-degree x4 41.6, out-degree /2 28.9, layers x2 43.4, layers /2 32.8. **Out-degree is what moves it**, which is the mechanism's own variable: how far down one shared queue a payer's budget reaches. The urn-ball limit depends on none of these, so it is not what is being read

criteria.detail: the unreached edges are the tail of each payer's own queue and not a set of edges. Across 4000 payers in 20 seeds every one sits in one of the two states the rule allows, 1739 reaching a prefix of its own ranked neighbours and stopping and 2220 reaching all of them, and there are **56 holes**, meaning 56 places where a payer reaches past an unreached counterparty. **The account registered before the run said that cannot happen, and it is wrong. Why is not established here.** The obvious explanation, that a counterparty which took in nothing has no capacity and the queue steps over it, is refuted by its own numbers: the largest capacity stepped over is 1.03e-27 while the smallest that absorbed anything is 3.88e-165, so being small is not what decides it. The diagnostic that looked like it settled this compared a last-round capacity against a mechanism that runs three hundred rounds, which is failure mode 130 over again. The allocation is clip(budget - ahead, 0, avail), so a counterparty is passed over when the capacity ahead of it exhausts the payer's budget in that round, and the run-level union of those rounds is what has to be printed. Registered and not run. So section eighteen's question, which edges make up the floor, has the answer that they are not identifiable as edges: they are wherever each payer's budget stops in a queue every payer walks in the same order. **What moves that stopping point is the payer's layer and not its out-degree.** Reached share by layer: l1 0.1970, l2 0.6513, mid 1.0000, a span of 0.8030, against 0.9231 across out-degrees whose relation is not monotone. The aggregate figure moves with out-degree (A26-21) while the per-payer relation does not, because the layers differ in degree and in budget at once
criteria.name: A26-22
